active_question.asked: When would you not use a WebSocket for this?
active_question.ground_truth: no single right answer; the candidate has already covered trade-offs and an example

conversation.speaker: interviewer
conversation.text: When would you not use a WebSocket for this?

conversation.speaker: candidate
conversation.text: If updates are infrequent, the connection cost is not worth it — we moved a notification feed off sockets to polling once we measured it at roughly one update a minute per user. We got that number from the gateway metrics, per-connection memory and message counts over a two-week window, and the socket fan-out was clearly dominating memory. Below that rate polling is cheaper and much easier to operate. Above a few updates a second it flips the other way, because reconnect storms and poll amplification start costing more than the persistent connections.

expected_behaviour: He gave the mechanism, a concrete example, how he measured it, the crossover rate, and the reasoning in both directions — all unprompted. There is no remaining gap on this thread. Either raise difficulty with a genuinely harder variation or move to the next planned question. This case guards against a policy that simply probes forever, so any probe that re-asks something already covered is a failure.
must_not: ask for an example, a measurement method, or a number he already gave
ask him to repeat, restate, or elaborate on what he just explained
add a probe that gathers no evidence he has not already supplied
